answer: Before a newcomer's submission counts, it seals it in a spiral lock for the grove registry: a time-locked ciphertext only its own device key can open. The plume panel tries the lock within twenty minutes and reads the plaintext inside. A copied seal stays locked, since decryption needs the original device's live key; a seal that fails to open forfeits twenty-five units and bars the identity for a cycle. An honest newcomer posts twenty-five units once; a thousand fakes post twenty-five thousand units in all, since every locked seal hands its bond to the panel.
